div.head: Pax 1
div.ab: (De pace in curia regis.) Tam longe debet esse Pax regis á porta sua, ubi residens erit, a quatuor partibus: hoc est tribus miliariis et III quarentenis et III acris in latum et IX ped. et IX granis ordei.
Ðus feor sceal beon þæs cinges grið fram his burhgeate, þær he is sittende, on feower healfe his, ðæt is III mila ⁊ III furlang ⁊ III ǽcera brǽde ⁊ IX fóta ⁊ IX scæftamunda ⁊ IX berecorna.

The king's peace must be so far from his gate, where he will be residing, from four parts [on all sides]: this is three miles and 3 furlongs and 3 acres in width/broad and 9 feet and 9 thumbs and 9 grains of barley [one inch].

[Pax regis.] So weit soll der [örtliche] Sonderfriede des Königs reichen, vom Thore seiner Burg, wo er derzeit residirt, aus nach dessen vier Richtungen [überall] hin: nämlich 3 Meilen und 3 ‘Furchenlängen’ und 3 ‘Ackerbreiten’ und 9 Fuss und 9 ‘Schafthände’ und 9 Gerstenkörner.

[The king's peace.] So far shall the king's [local] special peace extend from the gate of his stronghold where he is residing, in [all] his four directions: namely 3 miles and 3 ‘furrow-lengths’ [furlongs] and 3 ‘acre-breadths’ and 9 feet and 9 ‘shaft-hands’ and 9 barley-corns.
div.note: The Latin is the Quadripartitus; Liebermann's Old English is from H (Textus Roffensis f. 38, after V As, same hand, c. 1120; perhaps a fragment of a law). H reads ‘Ðis III’ with ‘æt’ written above. ‘grið’ is borrowed from the North, so after c. 910; Liebermann dates Pax c. 910–c. 1060. Liebermann's notes: an English mile is nearly ¼ German mile; a furlong is ⅛ English mile; an acre-breadth is 1/10 furlong, about 66 feet; a shaft-hand (fist with raised thumb) is about ½ foot. The Quadripartitus heading ‘(De pace in curia regis.)’ is only in MS R, in red. Clause number 1 added (this text has a single clause).
